stories_overflow.reason: Agentic multimodal scientific foundation model work intersects with agentic-system attack surfaces and long-horizon reasoning, relevant for security analysis though not focused on adversarial robustness.

stories_overflow.title: DreamGuard: Efficient Runtime Guardrail for LLM Agents via Risk-Aware World Model
stories_overflow.summary: DreamGuard is a proactive runtime guardrail for LLM agents that uses a risk-aware world model to track a compact recurrent latent state over trajectories and forecast future latent states. From these forecasts, it derives immediate-hazard and prefix-risk evidence and fuses multi-horizon signals to decide on interventions before tool executions. Across four benchmarks and an online evaluation, DreamGuard outperforms generic, reactive, and proactive baselines with the best safety-utility trade-off and averages 25 ms end-to-end latency per call.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Introduces a trajectory-aware, low-latency guardrail with explicit risk modeling, aligning with interests in long-horizon safety for LLM agents and bridging to sequence modeling ideas from time series foundation models.
stories_overflow.reason: Adaptive allocation across model populations for LLM-driven evolutionary search is relevant for cost-efficient red-teaming/evolutionary program search, but more about budgeting than core security.

stories_overflow.title: SkillTFM: Gated Skill Evolution for Training-Free Adaptation of Tabular Foundation Models
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces SkillTFM, a training-free adaptation system for tabular foundation models that replaces parameter updates with gated evolution of agentic skills. It uses a verifiable, extensible skill bank combining boundary evidence identification to characterize task structure and base-model failures with gated skill evolution to retrieve and extend reusable skills under explicit validation. In simulated boundary settings and real-world electricity-price forecasting, SkillTFM improves AUC by 0.128–0.142, elevating nonlinear-boundary AUC from 0.699 to 0.898, and shows effectiveness across different TFM backbones.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It proposes a security-adjacent, verifiable skill-gating mechanism for training-free adaptation under distribution shift, echoing modular skill libraries and guarded tool-use in LLMs while targeting tabular/time-series TFMs.
stories_overflow.reason: Empirical study of self-pretraining for medical time series—useful data on pretraining benefits and transfer in noisy, multimodal TS settings though domain-specific.

stories_overflow.title: Learning the Pareto Frontier of Predictive Models under Distribution Shift
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces Frontier Learning, which treats a library of pretrained models with mixed access regimes (black-box predictions and white-box representations) as complementary sources under distribution shift. It builds a unified target-domain feature by concatenating internal representations from white-box models with outputs from black-box models, then trains a lightweight regularized supervised learner, guaranteeing training-sample risk no worse than any single baseline including zero-shot reuse, fine-tuning, or direct training. Experiments on simulations and real-world shifts (DomainNet/VisDA and MIMIC-IV-Notes ICU mortality) show it matches or outperforms the strongest individual reuse strategy, with the largest gains when no single baseline is reliable across the shifts considered.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Provides a simple, access-agnostic ensemble-on-representations approach that subsumes common reuse strategies and is empirically strong under shift—relevant to robustness/security and modular reuse of foundation models.
stories_overflow.reason: Agentic BO using LLMs to inject priors into optimization touches on agentic systems and leveraging LLMs as components—relevant to attack/defense surfaces and efficient automated red-teaming workflows.

stories_overflow.title: Taxonomy-Driven Analysis of Open-Source AI Risk Mitigation Tools
stories_overflow.summary: The paper presents a taxonomy-driven protocol that uses an LLM-assisted RAG pipeline to map capabilities of 21 open-source LLM evaluation and security tools to 32 subcategories of the extended MIT AI Risk Mitigation and Response Taxonomy. The study finds a skewed tooling landscape concentrated on technical and operational controls, with major gaps in governance, legal/regulatory, and financial/market controls, and reports moderate inter-rater reliability (Fleiss’ Kappa = 0.509) and an F1 score of 75.5% after majority voting. It proposes a layered risk-mitigation architecture that combines tool-based controls with organizational and regulatory processes and offers a practical mapping highlighting where human oversight is still needed.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Gives a concrete, reproducible mapping from OSS LLM security/eval tools to a recognized risk taxonomy, clarifying coverage gaps relevant to red teaming, guardrails, and trust pipelines for foundation models (including time-series variants).
stories_overflow.reason: Using VLMs to encode time-series as images speaks to practical efficiency and cross-modal approaches for time-series analysis and could impact deployment/serving costs for TS workloads.

stories_overflow.title: LabelFusion-TS: Fusing Large Language Models, Transformer Encoders, and Financial Time Series for Monetary-Policy Stance Classification
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces LabelFusion-TS, which combines a fine-tuned RoBERTa encoder, a prompted LLM, and an ensemble of time-series transformers over pre-publication market series via a small voting network to classify FOMC sentences as hawkish, dovish, or neutral. Due to limited human labels (~1k sentences), the RoBERTa encoder is first pre-trained on LLM-generated weak labels and then fine-tuned on human annotations. Trained on data up to 2015 and evaluated on 2015–2022, the fused system attains 70.2% weighted F1, surpassing a zero-shot LLM at 64.1% and overtaking it with as few as 240 human-labeled sentences.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It demonstrates measurable gains from fusing market time series with LLM/text encoders for monetary-policy stance classification, highlighting a practical multimodal path beyond text-only classifiers.
stories_overflow.reason: Multimodal fusion of financial time series with LLMs for stance classification touches the reader's TSFM interest (benchmarks/architectures) and evaluation, though it's a narrow financial NLP application.

stories_overflow.title: Analysis of Federated Aggregation under Model Poisoning and Backdoor Attacks: A Reconstructed Cross-Dataset and Cross-Architecture Benchmark
stories_overflow.summary: This work reconstructs a 500-cell federated aggregation benchmark across five methods, five datasets, five architectures, and four conditions (clean, sign-flipping, Gaussian, BadNets), recovering 454 original runs and 36 repairs/reruns, with 10 SVHN cells covered only by summary provenance. Trimmed Mean has the best clean macro-mean accuracy and lowest mean within-task rank, while Krum shows the top recorded accuracy under sign-flipping and Gaussian, and these rankings persist when restricted to fully logged task pairs. Audits reveal the BadNets metric is actually TTLR (all test inputs triggered) and a FedPARETO pathway where reported predictive summaries may not match the corrupted updates used for aggregation, so results are descriptive within recorded configs rather than universal robustness claims.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Highlights reproducibility gaps, metric mis-specification (TTLR), and aggregation/provenance pitfalls that can confound robustness claims in federated settings relevant to secure FL and poisoning/backdoor evaluation.
stories_overflow.reason: Cross‑dataset benchmark for federated aggregation under poisoning/backdoors informs robust evaluation and threat models though it's more federated learning than LLM‑specific.

stories_overflow.title: GCPO: Diagnosing and Constraining Subspace Geometry in Rollout RL for LLMs
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces Principal-Subspace Overlap, a dimension-corrected metric quantifying how individual rollout updates align with dominant singular subspaces of pretrained LLM weights, and observes transient overlap spikes that precede performance degradation despite low averages. It proposes GCPO, which applies hard bilateral orthogonal projections to constrain updates to complementary subspaces, preventing such excursions by construction. Across reasoning, coding, and tool-use tasks on Qwen3-8B and GLM4-9B, GCPO outperforms GRPO and variants (DAPO, GSPO), improves over base and strongest baselines by up to 27.69 and 2.37 points, and preserves general capability, eliminates response-length inflation, and stabilizes policy entropy.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Offers a concrete geometric diagnostic and a projection-based control mechanism that stabilizes rollout RL for LLMs while improving performance and mitigating common failure modes like length inflation.
stories_overflow.reason: Systems paper on batching and avoiding host round trips in LLM-agent control; relevant for scalable agent deployment and attack surface (tool-call handling) in agentic systems.

stories_overflow.title: Into the ORBIT for Time Series: Training Regimes for Foundation Models
stories_overflow.reason: Evaluation metric for synthetic limit-order-book time series is relevant for TSFM evaluation and assessing generative-model fidelity, with potential security implications for market-simulation attacks.

stories_overflow.reason: SpecRoll focuses on speculative decoding within RL rollouts to speed generation—relevant for efficient agentic RLHF/rollouts but not directly on LLM security or time-series foundations.

stories_overflow.title: PolicyKG: An Agentic LLM Pipeline for Translating Institutional Policies into SHACL Knowledge Graphs
stories_overflow.reason: Practical pipeline for translating policies into formal constraints using LLMs and validators touches agentic system tooling and automated compliance verification, useful for governance/evaluation of agent behavior.

stories_overflow.reason: Diffusion model merging backdoor mitigation is solid adversarial-ML work but targets generative image models rather than LLMs or time-series models—peripheral relevance for methodology.

stories_overflow.reason: IoT firmware vulnerability detection benchmark is relevant to broader adversarial robustness and benchmark validity but outside core LLM/security or time‑series focus.

stories_overflow.reason: Theoretical unification of generative models via path integrals is mathematically interesting and could inform sampling/robustness, but it's distant from the user's priority areas (LLM security and TSFM).

llm-security.description: Attacks, defenses, and evaluation of LLM systems: jailbreaks, prompt injection, data extraction, red-teaming, alignment-adjacent safety failures with a security framing.

items.title: BASIS: Breach-Aware Selective Prompt Injection Shielding with Prefill Attention Probes
items.summary: The paper addresses over-refusal in prompt-injection defenses by noting that aligned models with robust instructions can withstand many injections, so blanket detection-and-refuse strategies are suboptimal. It proposes BASIS, which uses Attention Competition Ratio features to train two sparse linear probes—an existence probe and a breach probe—that operate in a cascaded, no-extra-inference gating pipeline to detect injections, predict per-sample breaches, and assess instruction robustness. Experiments on four tasks and six open-source LLMs report near-perfect injection detection with substantially reduced over-refusal on safe attack samples, particularly when using robust instruction templates.
items.why_it_matters: It introduces a lightweight, prefill-attention–based, per-sample breach predictor that can cut false refusals without extra LLM calls, complementing existing prompt-injection defenses and aligning with selective prediction ideas familiar from LLM safety and reliability.
items.reason: Persistent semantic entities expose long-lived, cross-boundary contamination in tool-augmented agents — directly relevant to agentic attack surfaces, memory poisoning, and debugging for security.

items.title: Agent Against Agent: An Agentic System for Automatic Prompt Injection Red Teaming
items.summary: The paper proposes PIMiner, an agentic red-teaming system for prompt injection that trains over sequences of (dataset, target model) pairs to build a strategy library from scratch. At test time, it transfers this library to unseen target LLMs without additional training and uses only a small number of target-agent queries per sample (e.g., 10). Experiments show strong ASR on IPIArena (76.2% Gemini-2.5-Pro, 61.9% GPT-5.1, 42.9% Claude-Sonnet-4.5) and AgentDojo (86.7% Gemini-2.5-Pro, 53.3% GPT-5.1, 40.0% Claude-Sonnet-4.5), outperforming RL-based approaches that generalize poorly.
items.why_it_matters: Offers a transferable, query-efficient prompt-injection attacker that challenges current RL-based red teaming and provides high-quality adversarial data for evaluating and training agent defenses.
items.reason: Automated agentic prompt-injection red teaming addresses prompt-injection attacks and scalable red-team data collection — directly targets core LLM security interests and practical evaluation.

items.title: HarnessSafe: Evaluating Safety Across Persistent Carriers in Agent Harnesses
items.summary: The paper introduces HarnessSafe, a benchmark of 328 executable cases spanning seven persistent-carrier families to assess delayed safety risks in agent harnesses that persist state across tasks and sessions. Each case is defined as a Persistent-Risk Lifecycle that traces attacker influence from entry through cross-carrier persistence to a benign trigger and an observable violation, and a multi-stage, trace-based evaluation measures how far each attack progresses and where it is stopped. Experiments indicate containment is carrier-specific and depends strongly on the harness-model configuration, with both harness and model shaping outcomes and attack success rates failing to capture lifecycle progression patterns.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a carrier-aware, trace-based methodology and dataset to dissect how safety risks propagate across memory/tools/skills in agentic systems—complementing coarse success-rate metrics and informing defense design in LLM agents and persistent pipelines.
items.reason: Benchmarks delayed safety risks from persistent carriers in agent harnesses; directly targets attack surfaces (memory, tools, skills), evaluation methodology, and end-to-end exploit propagation — highly relevant to LLM security and agentic threat models.

items.title: Matryoshka Language Model Suites
items.summary: The paper introduces a Matryoshka training framework that nests sub-models of increasing size into one end-to-end trained architecture, reducing total suite parameters and enabling step-wise distillation from the largest to all smaller sub-models. This structure is well-suited for speculative decoding because the draft model is contained within the verifier. A 500M/1.5B/3B suite matches independently trained baselines on benchmarks and perplexities while using 36% less training compute and yielding 14–26% higher speculative decoding throughput, with ablations provided on architectural choices.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a practical path to multi-size LLM suites that cut training/inference cost and improve speculative decoding, directly relevant to secure, efficient deployment pipelines and scalable time-series/LLM hybrid stacks.
items.reason: Direct audit showing internal harmfulness scores can anti-rank successful jailbreaks—highly relevant to guardrail evaluation, false-positive budgeting, and deployment filtering.

items.title: Toward Metacognitive One-Shot Indirect Prompt Injection: Strategy Abstraction Via Outcome-Conditioned Reflection
items.summary: The paper introduces SAVOR, a one-shot IPI attack framework that moves adaptation offline via outcome-conditioned reflection over successful and failed trajectories from disjoint training environments, consolidating validated, context-conditioned strategies into a reusable strategy memory. At test time, the frozen memory generates a single payload per unseen target without iterative interaction or feedback, achieving the highest average attack success rate across two benchmarks and three victim models. On Agent Security Bench and the new executable OpenClaw-IPI, SAVOR outperforms the strongest prior attack by 2.5–11.8 points and beats the same injection channel without strategy learning by 23.1 and 28.6 points respectively, with learned memory transferring across defenses.
items.why_it_matters: Demonstrates practical one-shot IPI via offline strategy distillation that generalizes across tools, goals, and defenses—relevant for red-teaming LLM agents and for designing defenses that hold under realistic single-interaction constraints.
items.reason: One-shot indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks on tool-using agents via offline strategy distillation directly targets agentic attack surfaces and realistic attacker models—highly relevant to LLM security and red-teaming methodology.

items.title: ElasticBack: Stealthy Conditional Backdoor in LLM-Agent Skills via Coupled Trigger-Rule Optimization
items.summary: The paper introduces ElasticBack, a conditional single-skill backdoor for LLM agents that couples a malicious rule R in the skill document with a benign-looking trigger T in user queries, activating only when both appear. It constructs R via semantic-anchored rule injection and then fixes R while evolving T using a stealth-constrained genetic search to optimize attack effectiveness and stealth without modifying model weights. Experiments over three target behaviors (50 skills each) and four agent LLMs show high ASR with near-zero FPR, preserved clean accuracy, cross-model transfer, and evasion of deployment-time defenses, motivating stronger supply-chain defenses for skills.
items.why_it_matters: Highlights a practical, weight-free, conditional backdoor vector in the emerging agent skill ecosystem, relevant to securing tool-using LLMs and evaluating defenses against stealthy trigger-rule couplings.
items.reason: Presents a stealthy conditional backdoor attack targeting agent skills (supply-chain threat) with low-cost single-skill triggers—highly relevant to LLM agent security, tool/skill poisoning, and defense evaluation.

items.title: Gradient Immunity: Null-Space Resistance to Malicious Fine-Tuning
items.summary: The paper targets the PPOW setting where most weights are trainable but a small safety-critical component is preserved, and proposes a Unidirectional Safety Gate implemented as a Null Space Cubic Layer plus an Inverse Adapter after the final Transformer layer. The cubic layer blocks or suppresses gradients from harmful samples whose hidden states lie within a calibrated protected region (threshold set using defender-held harmful data), while the Inverse Adapter restores the base model’s forward behavior. Across six model–dataset settings, this keeps post-finetuning attack success near pre-release levels under a fixed threshold, maintains high safe-pass on easier settings, and shows a clearer safety–utility trade-off on BeaverTails unsafe samples, indicating release-time representation-space blocking can raise the cost of malicious adaptation without downstream cooperation.
items.why_it_matters: Offers a concrete, release-time gradient-blocking mechanism that preserves forward behavior while resisting malicious fine-tuning—relevant to robust alignment under open-weight releases and complementary to gradient/representation-control methods in LLM safety.
items.reason: Direct defense proposal against malicious fine-tuning of released weights (PPOW setting) — highly relevant to LLM security, supply-chain attacks, and robustness of deployed models.

items.title: Understanding Backdoor Vulnerabilities in Vertical Federated Learning: The Gap Between Research and Practice
items.summary: This paper studies backdoor attacks in vertical federated learning, where asymmetric information lets initiators hide task details and contributors both poison training and trigger backdoors at inference. The authors argue prior near-perfect attack and defense results rely on unrealistic assumptions and flawed evaluation, revealing a research–practice gap in both methodological design and evaluation. They redefine realistic threat models, propose practical backdoor workflows, and release BVBench to enable fair, practical, and comprehensive evaluation with SOTA baselines, showing current understanding of VFL backdoor risks is fragile.
items.why_it_matters: It reframes VFL backdoor threat models and offers a benchmark (BVBench) to stress-test claims, informing more realistic security assessments relevant to LLM multi-party training and time-series feature-partitioned setups.
items.reason: Directly addresses training regimes for time-series foundation models, controlling pretraining distribution and targets — highly relevant to TSFM pretraining objectives, benchmarks, and transfer.

items.title: A Six-Dimensional Taxonomy of Post-Training Adaptation Techniques with Applications in AI Governance
items.summary: This survey synthesizes post-training adaptation techniques—spanning retraining, fine-tuning, parameter-efficient adaptation, alignment, RAG, model editing, unlearning, calibration, and multimodal instruction tuning—and introduces a six-dimensional taxonomy by mechanism, goal, data requirement, persistence, structural scope, and model type. It clarifies conflated terms (e.g., fine-tuning vs. RAG vs. prompting), traces the evolution of adaptation across model eras, and maps relationships such as inheritance, supersession, hybridization, and layered deployment stacks. The work presents a vocabulary to support technical documentation, change tracking, and governance analysis, and highlights open challenges in evaluation, reproducibility, persistent inference-time adaptation, unlearning, multimodal adaptation, and governance-aware workflows.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a governance-aligned taxonomy that can standardize how LLM security adaptations (e.g., alignment, unlearning, RAG) are described, compared, and tracked across deployment stacks, aiding reproducible evaluation and auditability.
items.reason: Presents a timestep-conditioned transformer for global weather forecasting addressing timestep choice trade-offs—directly relevant to TSFM pretraining/objectives and long-horizon forecasting design.

items.title: Personalized Federated Sparse Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
items.summary: The paper proposes a personalized federated sparse adaptation framework for TSFMs in building energy forecasting, using a heterogeneous temporal MoE adapter placed after the pretrained representation and a sequence-level router that assigns each 168-hour window to top-k experts specialized for distinct temporal structures. It evaluates global FL, local training, and personalized FL variants with globally shared vs client-private expert banks across 50 buildings and three TSFM backbones. Results show personalization consistently outperforms Global FL-MoE and Local MoE, the best sparse-adaptation strategy depends on backbone and metric, and routing reveals client-level expert specialization, expert concentration, and near-uniform routing across backbones, implying adaptation should be client- and backbone-aware.
items.why_it_matters: Combines federated personalization with sparse MoE routing for TSFMs under non-IID meter data, offering actionable design signals (client-/backbone-aware adapters) relevant to secure on-device adaptation and privacy-preserving deployment.
items.reason: Federated personalization for TS foundation models directly matches the reader's primary interest in TSFMs and on-device/private data adaptation; MoE adapter and sparse adaptation are relevant to architecture and efficient adaptation.

alignment.description: RLHF/RLAIF, preference learning, interpretability aimed at alignment, value learning, scalable oversight.

items.title: Do All LLMs Know When They're Being Harmful? A Reproducibility Study of Latent-Space Safety Probes Across Model Families
items.summary: This study reproduces Khatri et al.’s pipeline for training lightweight MLP probes on final-layer activations to detect harmful prompts, matching the original LLaMA-3.1-8B results within 0.37 F1 points (0.2 on BeaverTails). It extends the evaluation across Gemma-4-E4B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, and Qwen2-7B on WildJailbreak, BeaverTails, and AEGIS 2.0, finding F1 within about one point of the LLaMA-3.1-8B values using the same probe architecture. It also assesses nondeterminism by varying seeds and reports that final token latent vectors were invariant to seed across architectures.
items.why_it_matters: Suggests simple latent-space probes generalize across model families with stable activations, informing scalable, low-overhead safety detection for LLMs and complementing guardrail strategies.
items.reason: Reproducibility of latent safety probes across model families evaluates a lightweight detection approach that could scale as a defense or monitoring tool for harmful prompt detection.

items.title: Align-RAG: Alignment Is All You Need for TSFM In-Context Learning
items.summary: The paper introduces Align-RAG, a training-free method that applies closed-form amplitude rescaling and integer-lag phase alignment to retrieved past–future windows before feeding them to a frozen TSFM. On a frozen Chronos-Bolt, it outperforms a state-of-the-art trained retrieval adapter across seven benchmark datasets (average −3.75% MSE), and it also improves zero-shot MSE by 2.5%–13.7% on four additional frozen TSFMs without per-backbone tuning. Analysis shows aligned demonstrations induce prediction shifts in frozen backbones that track a closed-form ridge predictor on the same pairs, with a future-shuffle control ruling out futures-averaging, suggesting frozen TSFMs already support dynamic in-context use of retrievals.
items.why_it_matters: It challenges the need for learned fusion in RAG for forecasting by showing closed-form alignment on frozen backbones yields SOTA gains and ridge-like in-context adaptation, a strong baseline relevant to LLM alignment and retrieval studies.
items.reason: DASH improves on-policy self-distillation for reasoning models with temporally-adaptive supervision horizons — relevant to improving RL-style fine-tuning and evaluation of reasoning/judging behavior and scalable red-teaming.

items.title: Beyond Solvability: Task Learnability as a Static Prior for LLM RL Post-Training
items.summary: The paper introduces task learnability as a regime-conditional measure capturing how much tasks are expected to improve under a fixed LLM RL post-training setup, beyond snapshot solvability. They show learnability is reproducible across training contexts, predictive of downstream utility, and propose TrajVal, a probe-based estimator using a short probe run and two endpoint evaluations to approximate per-task learnability pre-training. TrajVal serves as a static prior for task sampling or as a multiplicative prior with online schedulers, improving data efficiency on math and logic benchmarks across model scales.
items.why_it_matters: Offers a practical, pre-training prior for task selection in RL post-training that complements online schedulers, improving compute allocation for reasoning tasks.

items.title: BASIS: Breach-Aware Selective Prompt Injection Shielding with Prefill Attention Probes
items.summary: The paper addresses over-refusal in prompt-injection defenses by noting that aligned models with robust instructions can withstand many injections, so blanket detection-and-refuse strategies are suboptimal. items.title: The Horizon Gap: Planning, Memory, Execution, Training, and Evaluation for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

items.title: HarnessSafe: Evaluating Safety Across Persistent Carriers in Agent Harnesses

items.title: Understanding Backdoor Vulnerabilities in Vertical Federated Learning: The Gap Between Research and Practice

items.title: A Six-Dimensional Taxonomy of Post-Training Adaptation Techniques with Applications in AI Governance

items.title: Deployable Per-Instance Multi-Layer Activation Steering for Large Language Models
items.summary: The paper shows that in activation steering, the optimal injection layers vary per input, with per-instance multi-layer selection outperforming any fixed global layer set across six binary persona traits on two 8B models. items.title: Personalized Federated Sparse Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models

items.title: Telemetry and Concealment in Self-Adapting Generative AI: Logging Architecture, Adversarial Model Hiding, and the Limits of Detection
items.summary: The paper addresses governance for self-updating generative models by proposing a telemetry architecture that operates in discrete and continuous time, including a Minimal Sufficient Statistic for audits, a Merkle-chain for discrete weight sequences, an Ito-based continuous-time generalization, and KL divergence stopping-time logging. It then formalizes the Model Hiding Problem under adversarial providers and catalogs six attack strategies against the telemetry architecture across discrete and continuous time, providing a countermeasure for each. The result is a dual-regime approach where continuous telemetry narrows but cannot replace periodic invasive audits, aligning with traditional MRM pillars and remaining architecture-agnostic.
items.why_it_matters: It offers concrete telemetry and adversarial-resilience mechanisms directly applicable to secure deployment and monitoring of self-adapting LLMs and time-series models where online weight updates break standard validation.

items.title: LoRAScan: Detecting Backdoor Prompts in Low-Rank Adapters for Large Language Models via Down-Projection Activation Spikes
items.summary: The paper introduces LoRAScan, an adapter-aware defense that detects and rejects trigger-bearing inputs for potentially backdoored LoRA adapters at inference time without modifying adapter parameters. It exploits the observation that about 5% of LoRA insertion sites exhibit stable activations on clean inputs but show concentrated spikes in down-projection activations when a trigger is present; these sites are identified pre-deployment and monitored online. On standard LLM backdoor benchmarks, LoRAScan rejects approximately 98.49 of malicious inputs with a small error rate on clean inputs, outperforming existing defenses across diverse settings.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a practical, deployment-compatible defense for LoRA-based supply-chain backdoors by leveraging activation signatures rather than adapter merging or retraining, aligning with current interests in robust LLM fine-tuning security.
items.reason: LoRAScan targets backdoored LoRA adapters—a direct supply-chain threat to LLM security (adapter-level backdoors) and practical detection method relevant to applied defenses.

items.title: Gradient Immunity: Null-Space Resistance to Malicious Fine-Tuning
items.summary: The paper targets the PPOW setting where most weights are trainable but a small safety-critical component is preserved, and proposes a Unidirectional Safety Gate implemented as a Null Space Cubic Layer plus an Inverse Adapter after the final Transformer layer. The cubic layer blocks or suppresses gradients from harmful samples whose hidden states lie within a calibrated protected region (threshold set using defender-held harmful data), while the Inverse Adapter restores the base model’s forward behavior. Across six model–dataset settings, this keeps post-finetuning attack success near pre-release levels under a fixed threshold, maintains high safe-pass on easier settings, and shows a clearer safety–utility trade-off on BeaverTails unsafe samples, indicating release-time representation-space blocking can raise the cost of malicious adaptation without downstream cooperation.
items.why_it_matters: Offers a concrete, release-time gradient-blocking mechanism that preserves forward behavior while resisting malicious fine-tuning—relevant to robust alignment under open-weight releases and complementary to gradient/representation-control methods in LLM safety.
items.reason: Direct defense proposal against malicious fine-tuning of released weights (PPOW setting) — highly relevant to LLM security, supply-chain attacks, and robustness of deployed models.

items.title: Measure, Don't Optimize: Forecasting Recovery in LLM Unlearning
items.summary: The paper introduces J-Access, an inference-time audit that projects intermediate representations into vocabulary space to measure how often target concepts remain accessible along the output pathway, hypothesizing that residual accessibility predicts recovery susceptibility. Auditing 398 public unlearned models across eight methods, they find most retain accessibility above a retain-only gold level, pre-attack accessibility predicts recovery speed and extent at the model level (but not per-fact), and directly minimizing J-Access causes the model to hide knowledge from the audit while increasing post-attack recovery. They conclude J-Access is useful as a model-level diagnostic for residual susceptibility and caution against turning internal audits into optimization targets without validation.

items.summary: The paper highlights that merging diffusion checkpoints can inherit dormant backdoors from compromised public sources while maintaining normal-looking generations, and mitigating this is hard without knowing the attacker specifics or sacrificing quality. items.title: Align-RAG: Alignment Is All You Need for TSFM In-Context Learning
items.summary: The paper introduces Align-RAG, a training-free method that applies closed-form amplitude rescaling and integer-lag phase alignment to retrieved past–future windows before feeding them to a frozen TSFM. On a frozen Chronos-Bolt, it outperforms a state-of-the-art trained retrieval adapter across seven benchmark datasets (average −3.75% MSE), and it also improves zero-shot MSE by 2.5%–13.7% on four additional frozen TSFMs without per-backbone tuning. Analysis shows aligned demonstrations induce prediction shifts in frozen backbones that track a closed-form ridge predictor on the same pairs, with a future-shuffle control ruling out futures-averaging, suggesting frozen TSFMs already support dynamic in-context use of retrievals.
items.why_it_matters: It challenges the need for learned fusion in RAG for forecasting by showing closed-form alignment on frozen backbones yields SOTA gains and ridge-like in-context adaptation, a strong baseline relevant to LLM alignment and retrieval studies.
items.reason: DASH improves on-policy self-distillation for reasoning models with temporally-adaptive supervision horizons — relevant to improving RL-style fine-tuning and evaluation of reasoning/judging behavior and scalable red-teaming.

items.title: Learning with Bilevel-Minimax Optimization for Efficient and Reliable Transfer Attacks
items.summary: The paper reframes transfer-based adversarial attacks as a bilevel-minimax problem, modeling the coupling among initialization, surrogate adaptation, and gradient-based perturbation optimization. It introduces BMAT, which uses a Soft Weight Modulator and an Implicit Gradient Approximator to enable ternary coupling and improve cross-architecture generalization, with accompanying theoretical analysis of the optimization dynamics. Experiments on classification and segmentation show BMAT outperforms 10+ baselines across 30+ victim models and can halve mIoU, with code released at the provided repository.
items.why_it_matters: Offers a principled bilevel-minimax view and practical solver that materially improves black-box transferability, relevant to robust LLM jailbreak defenses and cross-architecture time-series model attacks/defenses.
items.reason: Analyzes geometry of rollout RL for LLMs and proposes diagnostics/constraints — relevant to post‑training stability of LLM agents and rollout-based fine‑tuning used in safety work.
